content.title: About
content.content: Frozen cauliflower cooked with oil is a ready‑to‑eat product made from fresh cauliflower that is blanched, flash‑frozen and then sautéed in vegetable oil. It retains most of its nutrients and has a tender, slightly crisp texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cauliflower belongs to the cruciferous family, along with broccoli, Brussels sprouts and cabbage.
Freezing preserves up to 90 % of vitamin C, which is often lost in fresh produce during storage.
Cooking in oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K and carotenoids.
Cauliflower can be used as a low‑carb alternative to rice or potatoes in many dishes.
In the United States, frozen vegetables—including cauliflower—are among the top-selling ready‑to‑cook foods.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup provides about 70 kcal, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Compounds such as glucoraphanin help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Oil content
items.content: The product is prepared with vegetable oil, so those monitoring fat intake should consider its caloric contribution.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: A small number of people may be allergic to cruciferous vegetables.

items.title: Added salt or preservatives
items.content: Some versions may contain added salt or preservatives; check the label if this is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to heat: microwave or sauté briefly. Use it in soups, stews, pasta dishes, as a side dish, or as a base for vegetarian patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, consume within 2–3 days and do not refreeze.
